rule-01-1.label: Rule 01.1 Keep red off every party, side and person

rule-01-2.label: Rule 01.2 Draw every party in one neutral ink, with its name on the mark

rule-01-6.label: Rule 01.6 Show domes, columns and flags only in a captioned photograph of that place

rule-01-7.label: Rule 01.7 Keep party symbols, candidate photos, campaign gear and protest slogans out of brand graphics

rule-01-8.label: Rule 01.8 Photograph people doing public work, and caption who, what, where and when

rule-01-9.label: Rule 01.9 Draw no more than one example in four from one atlas domain, or one in five from one state

rule-01-10.label: Rule 01.10 Rotate examples across levels of government and regions

rule-01-14.label: Rule 01.14 Ask questions a supporter of the current rule could ask too

rule-01-15.label: Rule 01.15 Use plain verbs in place of war and sports metaphors

rule-01-16.label: Rule 01.16 Show both readings of a contested claim at the same length

rule-01-17.label: Rule 01.17 Describe a rule so its supporters would accept the description

rule-01-18.label: Rule 01.18 Set both halves of a hinge headline in one color and weight, and give the red to the ampersand

rule-01-19.label: Rule 01.19 Join people through a rule or place they share, and rotate their order

rule-01-20.label: Rule 01.20 Name parties, the left or the right in a hinge headline only to report sourced agreement

group-01-6.label: Group 6 Labels, Act pieces and names

rule-01-21.label: Rule 01.21 Open every kicker with one content label

rule-01-22.label: Rule 01.22 In a process piece, name the step and leave the side to the reader

rule-01-23.label: Rule 01.23 Put a position piece’s label before the headline and its fairness kit before the ask

rule-01-24.label: Rule 01.24 Name each product for what it does, and keep the ampersand for Oath & Action

group-02-1.label: Group 1 Sound like a person talking

rule-02-1.label: Rule 02.1 W01 Write it the way you would say it

rule-02-4.label: Rule 02.4 W04 Join thoughts that belong together

group-02-2.label: Group 2 Put the point first and stop

rule-02-5.label: Rule 02.5 W05 Open with something the reader can use

rule-02-6.label: Rule 02.6 W06 Give the point without a reveal

rule-02-7.label: Rule 02.7 W07 Stop when the facts stop

rule-02-8.label: Rule 02.8 W08 Close without a slogan

rule-02-12.label: Rule 02.12 W12 List what the facts hold

rule-02-13.label: Rule 02.13 W13 Give each sentence its own shape

rule-02-14.label: Rule 02.14 W14 Pull stacked nouns apart

rule-02-15.label: Rule 02.15 W15 Use the verb inside the noun

rule-02-16.label: Rule 02.16 W16 Drop the hedges and keep the grade

rule-02-19.label: Rule 02.19 W19 Let the facts carry the feeling

rule-02-21.label: Rule 02.21 W21 Leave out the em dash

rule-02-23.label: Rule 02.23 Set each brand line in its own place, word for word

rule-02-24.label: Rule 02.24 Close every piece on one next step, with its date

rule-02-25.label: Rule 02.25 Publish the mechanism behind a mood

rule-02-26.label: Rule 02.26 Use the words a reader would use, and spell series names exactly

rule-02-27.label: Rule 02.27 Write a hinge headline as a rule, then what it produces

rule-03-1.label: Rule 03.1 Place the wordmark from its master file

rule-03-2.label: Rule 03.2 Choose the lockup by the space and the surface

rule-03-3.label: Rule 03.3 Keep one cap height of clear space on every side

rule-03-5.label: Rule 03.5 Set the marks in their colors on the four approved surfaces

rule-03-7.label: Rule 03.7 Use L8 as the one monogram, and retire the spaced “O & A”

rule-03-8.label: Rule 03.8 Join a partner with a hairline, and keep our ampersand inside our name

rule-05-2.label: Rule 05.2 Set text only on color pairs that pass

fig-s-05-pairs.label: Every palette pair, measured, in chapter 05

rule-06-3.label: Rule 06.3 Set no text on screen below 13 px

rule-06-4.label: Rule 06.4 Tighten tracking only as headings grow

rule-06-5.label: Rule 06.5 Line up figures in tables, and give negatives the true minus sign

rule-06-6.label: Rule 06.6 Balance a heading’s lines, and keep two words or more on its last line

rule-06-7.label: Rule 06.7 Hang opening quotation marks outside the text edge

rule-06-8.label: Rule 06.8 Set body text at 60 to 75 characters a line

rule-06-9.label: Rule 06.9 Set email type in the system font stack

rule-07-3.label: Rule 07.3 Span body text across the columns that hold its measure

rule-07-5.label: Rule 07.5 Set breakpoints in em, so larger text gets fewer columns

rule-07-6.label: Rule 07.6 Make every page read at 320 px wide, with nothing lost

rule-08-2.label: Rule 08.2 Place the lockmark only in its four places, once in a view

rule-08-3.label: Rule 08.3 Let the lockmark code nothing
